$comment: Source strings for Cubeulator, British English. Each entry is key: [text, note for translators].
A text that is an object holds plural forms keyed 'one' and 'other'; %n is the count.
%1, %2 are placeholders. The inventory table in content.md and the prototype are generated from this file by tools/build.py.
Keys are stable ids: E2b turns them into qsTrId() ids. Never reuse a key for a different meaning.
app.name: Cubeulator
The product name. Never translated, never transliterated.
app.tagline: The headline on the home screen. Two lines. Short, confident. 'In your hands' means both 'you do the turning' and 'the cube is in your hands'; keep whichever sense reads naturally.
common.back: Button. Goes to the previous screen.
common.close: Button. Closes a sheet or dialog.
common.done: Button. Leaves a screen the person has finished with.
common.home: Button. Goes to the first screen.
common.openDeviceSettings: Button. Opens the operating system's settings, outside the app.
common.enterByHand: Button. Opens the screen where the cube's colours are typed in instead of scanned.
common.scanInstead: Button on the hand-entry screen. Switches to the camera.
common.more: Button. Opens a short list of less common actions.
common.carryOn: Button. Continue what was in progress. US: 'Continue'.
colour.white: A cube colour, as a label under a swatch.
colour.unset: Read out for a sticker whose colour has not been entered yet.
colourSide.white: A side of the cube is named by the colour of its centre sticker. Use the word for 'side', never 'face'.
mark.ring: The mark drawn on yellow stickers. Read by screen readers and used in Help.
mark.slash: The mark drawn on orange stickers: a short diagonal line.
mark.plus: The mark drawn on red stickers.
mark.dot: The mark drawn on green stickers.
mark.bar: The mark drawn on blue stickers.
side.top: Which side of the cube to turn, as the person holds it. Shown very large on the solve screen; keep it to one or two short words.
side.left: See side.top. The left-hand side of the cube.
side.right: See side.top. The right-hand side of the cube.
side.front: See side.top. The side facing the person.
side.back: See side.top. The side facing away from the person. Not the 'Back' navigation button: that is common.back.
dir.left: Which way to turn the top or bottom, from where the person is holding the cube. Never mirrored in right-to-left languages: it is the physical left.
dir.up: Which way to turn the left or right side: the part facing the person moves up.
dir.down: Which way to turn the left or right side: the part facing the person moves down.
dir.cw: Which way to turn the front or back, always as seen from the front.
dir.either: Shown for a half turn, where the direction does not matter.
dir.seenFromFront: Added under a turn of the back side, because the person cannot see it.
turn.U1: Turn the top a quarter turn to the left.
A whole instruction as one sentence. Read by screen readers and listed in Review the solution. 18 of these: six sides, three turns each.
turn.U3: Turn the top a quarter turn to the right.
turn.U2: Turn the top a half turn.
turn.D1: Turn the bottom a quarter turn to the right.
turn.D3: Turn the bottom a quarter turn to the left.
turn.D2: Turn the bottom a half turn.
turn.R1: Turn the right side a quarter turn upwards.
See turn.U1. Avoid any phrase that reads as the idiom 'right side up'.
turn.R3: Turn the right side a quarter turn downwards.
turn.R2: Turn the right side a half turn.
turn.L1: Turn the left side a quarter turn downwards.
turn.L3: Turn the left side a quarter turn upwards.
turn.L2: Turn the left side a half turn.
turn.F1: Turn the front a quarter turn clockwise.
turn.F3: Turn the front a quarter turn anticlockwise.
turn.F2: Turn the front a half turn.
turn.B1: Turn the back a quarter turn anticlockwise, as seen from the front.
turn.B3: Turn the back a quarter turn clockwise, as seen from the front.
turn.B2: Turn the back a half turn.
stage.1.title: White cross
Name of the first of five stages of the solve.
stage.1.what: Put the four white edge pieces on the bottom, each lined up with the colour of its side.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.1.why: Everything else is built on this cross.
Why this stage is done, for someone learning the method.
stage.2.title: White corners
Name of the second stage.
stage.2.what: Put the four white corners in place to finish the bottom layer.
stage.2.why: That is one whole layer solved, and it stays solved from here on.
stage.3.title: Middle layer
Name of the third stage.
stage.3.what: Put the four edge pieces of the middle layer in place.
stage.3.why: Two layers are then solved. Only the top is left.
stage.4.title: Yellow top
Name of the fourth stage. Cubers call it 'orienting the last layer'; do not use that phrase.
stage.4.what: Turn the top layer's pieces over until the whole top is yellow.
stage.4.why: The pieces are already in the top layer. This only turns them the right way up.
stage.5.title: Top layer in order
Name of the fifth stage. Cubers call it 'permuting the last layer'; do not use that phrase.
stage.5.what: Move the top layer's pieces round to their own places.
stage.5.why: They are the right way up but in the wrong order. Put them in order and the cube is solved.
stage.f2l.title: First two layers
Name of a stage the Intermediate method has instead of 'White corners' and 'Middle layer'. Cubers call it 'F2L'; do not use that term.
stage.f2l.what: Join each white corner to its middle-layer edge and put the pair in place, one pair at a time.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.reduce.title: Get it ready
Name of the first of two stages of the Advanced method. It does not look like progress: the cube is made ready for the second stage.
stage.reduce.what: Turn every piece the right way up and send the middle-layer edges back to the middle.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.finish.title: Finish
Name of the second of two stages of the Advanced method. Also the word on a button (solve.finish); here it is a heading.
stage.finish.what: Solve the rest with turns of the top and bottom and half turns of the other four sides.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.parity.title: Set up
Name of the first stage of a solve of a cube bigger than 3x3 when it needs one. Shown with a number, like the other stages. 'Parity' is the cuber's word; do not use it.
stage.parity.what: A few turns first, so that pairing up the pieces cannot leave two of them swapped, which only a big cube can do.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.centres.title: Centres
Name of a stage of a solve of a cube bigger than 3x3: gathering the middle stickers of each side.
stage.centres.what: Gather the middle stickers of each side into one block of a single colour.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.edges.title: Edges
Name of a stage of a solve of a cube bigger than 3x3: pairing the edge pieces.
stage.edges.what: Pair up the edge pieces into whole edges, so that the cube has twelve edges like a 3x3.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
stage.corners.title: Corners
Name of the only stage of a solve of a 2x2.
stage.corners.what: Put the eight corners where they belong. A 2x2 has nothing else.
What this stage does, in one sentence.
home.lede: Show your cube to the camera, then follow one turn at a time until it is solved.
One sentence under the headline on the home screen.
home.scan: The main button. Starts the camera.
home.history: Button. Opens the list of past solves.
home.other: Button on Home. Opens the screen for a cube the camera does not read: a different size, or a cube typed in as the scramble that mixed it up.
entry.title: Another cube
Title of the screen reached from Home by "Another size of cube".
entry.size.label: Size
Small heading above the buttons that choose the size of the cube: 2×2, 3×3 and so on.
entry.size.option: A size of cube on a button: the side length twice, as in 5×5. %1 is the number in the reader's own digits.
entry.size.camera: The camera reads this cube. Scan it, or type its scramble here.
Under the size buttons: the camera reads every size offered.
entry.scramble.label: Its scramble
Small heading above the box where the scramble is typed. A scramble is the list of moves that mixed the cube up, as a timer or a puzzle site shows it.
entry.scramble.placeholder: Type or paste the moves, such as R U R' U' F2 2R Rw
Grey text in the empty scramble box, showing what a scramble looks like. The moves are cubing notation and are not translated.
entry.scramble.help: Write the moves with a space between them. U' turns the other way and F2 is a half turn. 2R is the second layer in from R, and Rw turns two layers together.
Under the scramble box. The letters and marks are notation and stay as they are.
entry.solve: Main button of the screen for another size of cube. Works out the solution from the scramble.
entry.scan: Button shown when 3×3 is chosen. Goes to the camera.
entry.error.unknownMove: ‘%1’ is not a move. Moves look like R, U', F2, 2R or Rw.
Shown under the scramble box when a word in it is not a move. %1 is that word.
entry.error.layer: ‘%1’ turns a layer that a %2×%2 cube does not have.
Shown when a move names a layer the chosen size does not have, such as 5R on a 4×4. %1 is that move, %2 the size in the reader's own digits.
entry.error.empty: Shown when Solve it is pressed with nothing typed.
entry.error.solved: Those moves leave the cube as it was. Type a scramble that mixes it up.
Shown when the scramble turns the cube back to solved, so there is nothing to solve.
home.findingCamera: Shown briefly at start-up on a computer.
home.noCamera.title: No camera found
Heading of a notice.
home.noCamera.body: Plug one in and look again, or enter the colours by hand.
home.unsupported.title: Scanning is not ready on this device yet
Heading of a notice on a device whose camera this version cannot use.
home.unsupported.body: This version cannot use this device's camera. You can enter the colours by hand instead.
home.resume.title: Unfinished solve
Heading of a card offering to continue a solve that was left part-way.
home.resume.body: %1 is the turn reached, %2 the total. Both are numbers in the reader's own digits.
home.resume.discard: Button. Throws the unfinished solve away.
home.discard.title: Discard this solve?
Dialog title.
home.discard.body: You would need to scan the cube again to solve it.
firstRun.title: Solve your cube, one turn at a time
Headline of the welcome screen shown once, on first launch.
firstRun.step1.title: Scan
First of three numbered steps.
firstRun.step1.body: Show each of the cube's six sides to the camera.
firstRun.step2.title: Hold
Second step.
firstRun.step2.body: Prop this device up and hold the cube the way the picture shows.
Step body. 'This device' is a phone, tablet or computer.
firstRun.step3.title: Turn
Third step.
firstRun.step3.body: Follow one turn at a time until it is solved.
firstRun.need.title: You will need
Heading above a short list.
firstRun.need.cube: An ordinary 3x3 cube with coloured stickers and dark plastic between them.
List item. 3x3 means three squares along each edge.
firstRun.need.light: Bright, even light with no glare on the stickers.
firstRun.language: Button on the welcome screen. Opens the list of languages.
permission.title: Camera access
Screen title.
permission.body: Cubeulator reads your cube's colours through the camera.
permission.point1: The camera picture is used on this device only.
permission.point2: No picture is saved, uploaded or shared.
Reassurance. Must stay true: see docs/design/screens/privacy.md.
permission.point3: You can take access away again at any time in your device's settings.
permission.allow: Button. Makes the operating system show its own permission prompt.
permission.refused.title: Camera access is off
Screen title after the person refused, or when the device forbids it.
permission.refused.body: Cubeulator cannot scan without the camera. You can allow it in your device's settings, or enter the colours by hand.
permission.askAgain: Button. Tries the system prompt once more.
permission.system.camera: Cubeulator uses the camera to read the colours on your cube. Pictures stay on this device.
The reason shown by iOS and macOS inside their own permission prompt (NSCameraUsageDescription). One or two sentences.
scan.title.complete: Headline when all six sides are read and make a valid cube.
scan.guide.settling: Setting the camera's exposure and colour balance…
Guidance under the headline. Nothing is read while this shows.
scan.guide.first: Hold one side of the cube square to the camera
Guidance before any side is read. 'Square to' means facing it flat, not at an angle.
scan.guide.inView: Guidance when a side is seen but moving.
scan.guide.reading: Reading this side. Hold it there
Guidance while a side is being read.
scan.guide.next: Turn to a side that is not filled in below, square to the camera
Guidance between sides. 'Below' refers to the row of six small squares at the bottom of the screen.
scan.guide.seenBefore: This side is already read. Turn to another one
Guidance when the side shown has been read before.
scan.guide.conflict: These six sides do not make a valid cube yet. Show each side again, square to the camera.
Guidance when six sides are read but something is wrong.
scan.guide.ambiguous: These six sides fit together in more than one way. Turn the cube slowly so that two sides show at once.
Guidance when six sides are read and fit together in two ways, so that showing them again changes nothing. Turning the cube between sides, so that two sides are in view at once, settles which.
scan.guide.ambiguousCorner: Turn the cube slowly to show the corner where %1, %2 and %3 meet.

Guidance when six sides are read and fit together in more than one way, and showing one particular corner (two or three sides in one view) would tell the cubes they make apart. %1, %2 and %3 are the colours of the centres of the three sides that meet there - colour.white and the like, in no particular order. Shown in place of scan.guide.ambiguous, which says only that two sides should show at once.
scan.guide.complete: All six sides make a valid cube. Working out the solution…
Guidance when the scan has finished.
scan.guide.resuming: Starting the camera again. The sides already read are kept.
Guidance when the app comes back after being in the background.
scan.stuck.title: Not reading?
Heading of a hint that appears after ten seconds without progress.
scan.stuck.body: Use bright, even light. Tilt the cube until there is no glare on the stickers. Fill about half the picture with one side.
scan.startOver: Button. Forgets the sides read so far.
scan.size.auto: Button on the scan screen beside the sizes of cube: the app finds the size of the cube from what the camera sees.
scan.checkColours: Button. Opens the screen where each sticker can be corrected.
scan.more.chooseCamera: Item in the More sheet, on a computer with more than one camera.
scan.more.switchCamera: Item in the More sheet, on a phone: front or back camera.
scan.picker.title: Choose a camera
Title of the list of cameras.
scan.camera.none.title: No camera found
Headline.
scan.camera.none.body: Plug in a camera and look again, or enter the colours by hand.
scan.camera.busy.title: The camera is in use
Headline.
scan.camera.busy.body: Another program is using it. Close that program, then try again.
scan.camera.blocked.title: Camera access is blocked
Headline.
scan.camera.blocked.body: This device's settings do not let Cubeulator use the camera. Allow it there, then try again.
scan.camera.lost.title: The camera stopped
Headline.
scan.camera.lost.body: It may have been unplugged. The sides already read are kept.
scan.camera.failed.title: The camera could not start
Headline.
scan.camera.failed.body: Try again. If it keeps happening, report it with this code: %1
Guidance. %1 is a short error code such as E-CAM-12.
scan.solveFailed.title: No solution found
Headline. Rare.
scan.solveFailed.body: The cube was read, but Cubeulator could not work out how to solve it. Check the colours, or scan again.
scan.leave.title: Stop scanning?
Dialog title.

scan.leave.body.one: The side read so far will be lost.
scan.leave.body.other: The %n sides read so far will be lost.

scan.restart.title: Start over?
Dialog title.
scan.restart.keep: Dialog button: the safe choice. 'These' are the sides read so far.
scan.a11y.preview: Screen-reader name of the live camera view.
scan.a11y.sideRead: Announced by a screen reader each time a side is read.
scan.a11y.chipEmpty: Screen-reader name of an empty chip.
scan.a11y.chipRead: Screen-reader name of a filled chip. %2 is a colourSide string such as 'Red side'.
scan.a11y.chipInView: Side %1: read, and in view now. %2
Screen-reader name of the chip for the side currently shown to the camera.
scan.a11y.cubeSeen: Announced once when the camera first sees a side.
review.title.check: Screen title when checking a scan.
review.title.enter: Screen title when entering a cube by hand.
review.intro.enter: Pick a colour, then tap each sticker of that colour. Do one side at a time. It does not matter which way up you hold each side.
Instruction at the top of hand entry.
review.intro.check: Compare each side with your cube. Tap a colour, then tap any sticker that is wrong.
Instruction at the top when checking a scan.
review.intro.enterN: Hold your cube any way up. Call the side facing up the top and the side facing you the front. Pick a colour, then tap or drag over the stickers of that colour on the side shown. The sides named round it are the ones against its edges.
Instruction at the top of entering a cube of any size by hand. Replaces review.intro.enter for a cube that has no centre sticker to name each side by.
review.centre: The centre never changes. It names the side.
Shown when the person taps a centre sticker, which cannot be edited.
review.palette: Screen-reader name of the row of six colour buttons.
review.sidePicker: Screen-reader name of the row of six side buttons.
review.status.empty: Status line before anything is entered. A cube has 54 stickers; the six centres are already set.
review.status.emptyN: Status line before anything is entered, for a cube of any size. %1 is how many stickers the cube has, in the reader's own digits.
review.fault.noScheme: These colours cannot be the six sides of one cube.
Says what is wrong with colours that fit in no cube: two colours that belong on opposite sides sit next to each other.
review.fault.centreColours: The middle stickers of a side do not hold each colour equally often.
Says what is wrong when the middle stickers of one side's ring have the wrong mix of colours.
review.fault.unknownPiece: A piece shows colours that no piece of a cube has.
Says what is wrong when a corner or an edge has two colours that are never next to each other.
review.fault.repeatedPiece: Two pieces show the same colours, so another piece is missing.
Says what is wrong when the same corner or edge is entered twice.
review.fault.twistedCorner: A corner looks turned in place.
Says what is wrong when the corners are right but one is twisted.
review.fault.flippedEdge: Says what is wrong when the edges are right but one has its two colours the wrong way round.
review.fault.swappedPieces: Says what is wrong when two pieces are in each other's places.
review.clearAll: Button at the top of the hand-entry screen. Unsets every sticker of every side.
review.fillSide: Button under the colours on the hand-entry screen. Paints every sticker of the side being edited with the colour chosen.
review.status.miscount: The colours do not add up
Status headline when some colour is used more or fewer than nine times.
review.status.miscountOver: %1 is a list such as 'Red (10), Blue (11)'.
review.status.miscountUnder: %1 is a list such as 'Orange (8), Green (7)'.
review.status.countItem: One item in those lists. %1 is a colour name exactly as in colour.*, %2 how many stickers have it.
review.status.impossible: This cannot be a real cube
Status headline when every colour appears nine times but the pieces do not fit together.
review.status.impossibleBody: One sticker is probably on the wrong piece. Check each side against your cube again.
review.status.valid: Status headline when the colours make a cube that can be solved.
review.solve: The main button. Works out the solution.
review.clearSide: Button. Unsets the eight stickers round the centre of the side being edited.
review.failed.title: No solution found
Headline. Rare.
review.failed.body: Cubeulator could not work out how to solve this cube. Try again, or scan it instead.
review.discard.title: Discard these colours?
Dialog title.
review.discard.body: What you have entered will be lost.
review.a11y.sticker: Screen-reader name of one sticker. %1 is a colourSide string, %2 and %3 are 1 to 3, %4 a colour name or colour.unset.
review.a11y.sideDone: Screen-reader name of a side button when all nine stickers are set. %1 is a colourSide string.
review.a11y.sideLeft: Screen-reader name of a side button. %1 is a colourSide string.
review.notUpright: The camera could not tell which way up each side was held, so each is shown as it saw it. Compare every side with your cube, and turn any that is the wrong way round.

Shown on the check screen when the camera named the colours of the sides but could not fit them together into a cube, so it does not know which way up each side was held. Each side is shown as the camera saw it and may need turning (review.turnSide).

review.doubt.note.one: The camera was not sure of %n sticker. It is marked with a ?.
review.doubt.note.other: The camera was not sure of %n stickers. They are marked with a ?.

review.doubt.note: Shown on the check screen when the camera was unsure of some stickers. %n is how many. The mark is a question mark drawn on the sticker itself; keep the question mark as the plain Latin character.
review.a11y.stickerUnsure: %1, row %2, column %3: %4. The camera was not sure of this one.
Screen-reader name of a sticker the camera was unsure of. Like review.a11y.sticker, with the extra sentence. %1 is a colourSide string, %2 and %3 are 1 to 9, %4 a colour name or colour.unset.
review.undo: Button on the colours screen. Takes back the last change.
review.redo: Button on the colours screen. Puts back the change that Undo took back.
review.revert: Button on the check screen. Puts every sticker back as the camera read it, taking back all the corrections made here. Undo can bring them back.
review.turnSide: Button on the colours screen. Turns the side being edited a quarter turn clockwise, as seen from outside, in the picture only: for a side the camera read the wrong way up. It does not turn the cube.
review.describe.open: Button on the colours screen. Opens a box to type the colours of the whole side as letters instead of tapping each sticker.
review.describe.help: Type the colours of this side (%1) as you see it on your cube, left to right, a row at a time: W white, Y yellow, G green, B blue, O orange, R red. Use ? for a sticker you cannot tell. Spaces and slashes are ignored.

Instruction above the box where a side is described in letters. %1 is the side's name (colourSide.red, side.top and the like). The letters W Y G B O R are fixed, like the letters of a move, and are not translated; say in the language which colour each stands for, naming the colours as in colour.*.
review.describe.field: Colours of this side, as letters
Screen-reader name of the box where a side is described in letters.
review.describe.apply: Button under the box where a side is described in letters. Paints the side with what was typed.
review.describe.tooFew: That is only %1 of the %2 colours this side needs.
Shown when the description of a side has too few colours. %1 is how many were typed and %2 how many stickers the side has, in the reader's own digits.
review.describe.tooMany: That is %1 colours, but this side has only %2 stickers.
Shown when the description of a side has too many colours. %1 is how many were typed and %2 how many stickers the side has, in the reader's own digits. %1 is always larger than %2.
review.describe.unknownLetter: ‘%1’ is not a colour. Use W, Y, G, B, O or R, or ? for a sticker you cannot tell.
Shown when the description of a side has a letter that is no colour. %1 is that letter. The letters W Y G B O R are fixed and not translated.
solve.working: Shown while the solution is computed.
solve.failed.title: No solution found
Headline. Rare.
solve.failed.body: Cubeulator could not work out how to solve this cube. Check the colours, or scan it again.
solve.alreadySolved.title: This cube is already solved
Headline when a solved cube is scanned.
solve.alreadySolved.body: There is nothing to do. Mix it up and scan it again.
solve.hold.title: Hold the cube like this
Headline of the step before the first turn.
solve.hold.body: Yellow centre on top. Green centre facing you. Keep it this way round for the whole solve.
solve.hold.match: Your cube should match the picture.
Line under the picture of the cube.
solve.hold.ready: I am holding it like this
The main button. Starts the first turn.
solve.hold.check: Something looks wrong? Check the colours
solve.holdResume.title: Carry on from turn %1
Headline when returning to an unfinished solve.
solve.holdResume.body: Hold the cube with the yellow centre on top and the green centre facing you. It should match the picture.
solve.differs: Button. Opens advice for when the cube and the picture disagree.
solve.holdLine: Yellow on top · green facing you
A reminder that stays on the solve screen the whole time. Keep it short. The dot is a separator.
solve.progress: Progress through the solve. Numbers in the reader's own digits.
solve.stageOf: Which stage of this solution is being worked on, and how many it has: five for Beginner, four for Intermediate, two for Advanced. Shown in small capitals.
solve.next: The main button on the solve screen. Very large.
solve.previous: Button. Undoes the last turn on screen so the person can undo it on the cube.
solve.move.layer: The move in words for a layer inside a cube bigger than 3x3. %1 is the side, as 'Right side' or 'Top'; %2 is how far in the layer is counted from that side, starting at 1 for the outer layer; %3 is 'quarter turn' or 'half turn'. The dots are separators.
solve.move.layers: The same for several layers turned together. %2 and %3 are the nearest and the farthest layer, counted from the side as above; %4 is 'quarter turn' or 'half turn'.
solve.skipToCore: Button on the solve screen of a cube bigger than 3x3. Jumps over the stages that pair up its pieces.
solve.skipToCore.note: Use this once you have paired up the centres and edges yourself. The cube on screen jumps to the 3x3 it should now be.
Explains the button above it, for someone who can already solve a 3x3.
solve.method.finishWith: Small label above the three method buttons when the cube is bigger than 3x3: the methods apply to the 3x3 the cube has become, so they are said to be how it is finished.
solve.finish: Replaces 'Next turn' on the last turn.
solve.hint.touch: Make the turn, then tap the cube.
Shown once, on the first turn of a first solve, on touch devices.
solve.hint.keys: Make the turn, then press Space.
The same, on a computer. 'Space' is the space bar.
solve.stageDone.title: %1 done
Headline between stages. %1 is a stage title such as 'White cross'.
solve.stageDone.check: Check your cube matches the picture.
Line asking the person to compare.
solve.paused: Title of the pause menu, and of the paused state in timer mode.
solve.menu.leaveNote: Your place is kept. Carry on from Home.
solve.lost.title: Cube and picture do not match
Headline.
solve.lost.body: One turn probably went the wrong way. Try these in order.
solve.lost.step1: Check how you are holding it: yellow centre on top, green centre facing you.
solve.lost.step2: Go back one turn and compare again.
solve.lost.step3: Scan the cube again. Cubeulator solves it from where it is now.
solve.a11y.menu: Screen-reader name of the menu button on the solve screen.
solve.a11y.cube: The cube as it should look now. %1
Screen-reader description of the picture of the cube. %1 is the current turn sentence.
solve.a11y.progress: Read when the turn changes. %3 is a stage title.
solve.a11y.notation: Read after the turn sentence when notation is switched on. %1 is letters such as R' or U2; do not translate it.
solve.method.beginner: Name of the first way of solving a cube: layer by layer. A button label, one word.
solve.method.intermediate: Name of the second way of solving: the way fast solvers do it, in four stages. A button label, one word.
solve.method.advanced: Name of the third way of solving: the fewest turns, with no stages to learn. A button label, one word.

solve.method.intermediate.note: The way fast solvers do it, in four stages. About 50 turns.
One line under the three method buttons, shown while Intermediate is chosen. 'About 50' is an average; keep it approximate.
solve.method.advanced.note: The fewest turns there are, with no stages to learn. About 20 turns.

diagnostics.markerFrames: Writing diagnostics and camera frames to %1
Developer builds only. As diagnostics.marker, when camera frames are being kept as well. %1 is the folder the diagnostics are written to.

help.title: Help
Screen title.
help.lost: If the cube does not match
help.scanning.body:
Hold the cube so that one side faces the camera flat, filling about half the picture.

Keep it still until that side appears in the row at the bottom. Then turn to another side. The order does not matter, and it does not matter which way up each side is.

Use bright, even light. If a sticker shines, tilt the cube a little until the shine goes. A window behind you is better than a window behind the cube.

If a side will not read, you can enter the colours by hand.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences.
help.entering.body:
Choose a colour, then tap every sticker of that colour on the side you are looking at. Then choose the next colour.

Do one side at a time. The centre of each side is filled in already: it never changes, and it tells you which side you are on.

It does not matter which way up you hold each side. Cubeulator works that out.

When every sticker is filled in, Cubeulator checks that the colours make a real cube. If they do not, compare each side with your cube again.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences. The third paragraph is true only if the scan lane accepts a side in any rotation; see screens/review.md.
help.holding.body:
For the whole solve, hold the cube the same way round: the side with the yellow centre on top, the side with the green centre facing you.

Look at the centres only. The other stickers move; the centres never do.

After a turn, do not turn the whole cube round to look at it. If you do, put it back: yellow centre on top, green centre facing you.

Prop this device up where you can see it with both hands on the cube.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences.
help.turns.body:
A side is one of the six sides of the cube. Each is named by where it is as you hold it: top, bottom, left, right, front and back.

A turn moves one side a quarter of the way round, or half way.

The top and bottom turn to the left or to the right. The left and right sides turn upwards or downwards: that is the way the part facing you moves. The front and back turn clockwise or anticlockwise, always as you see it from the front.

The picture shows every turn. If the words and the picture ever seem to disagree, follow the picture.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences. Use exactly the words chosen for side.*, dir.* and amount.*.
help.lost.body:
If your cube stops matching the picture, one turn has probably gone the wrong way.

First check how you are holding it: yellow centre on top, green centre facing you.

Then go back one turn and compare again.

If it still does not match, scan the cube again. Cubeulator solves it from where it is now, so nothing is lost but a little time.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences.
help.cubes.body:
Cubeulator works with an ordinary 3x3 cube: nine coloured stickers on each side, with dark plastic between them, in white, yellow, red, orange, green and blue.

It does not yet read cubes without stickers, cubes made of white or light plastic, cubes with pictures, or cubes in other colours. You can still enter one of those by hand if its six colours can be matched to the six here.

It does not work with other sizes of cube.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences.
help.notation.body:
Cubers write turns as letters. Cubeulator can show them beside its own words: turn on Show cube notation in Settings.

U is the top, D the bottom, L the left, R the right, F the front and B the back.

A letter alone is a quarter turn clockwise, as you would see it looking straight at that side. An apostrophe after it means anticlockwise. A 2 means a half turn.

That is why the bottom and the back can seem to go the wrong way: in notation, clockwise is judged from underneath and from behind. Cubeulator's own words are always from where you are.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences. Do not translate the letters U, D, L, R, F, B.
help.keys.body:
On the solve screen, Space, Enter or Page Down moves to the next turn. Page Up goes back one. P pauses. Esc leaves and keeps your place.

Everywhere, Tab moves to the next control, Space or Enter presses it, and Esc goes back.

F1 opens Help.
Body of a Help topic. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Keep the short sentences. Computers only. Key names stay in English unless the keyboards sold in your country print them differently.
